purpose: Decide how a subscription bookkeeping practice takes a signed client from unknown books to a repeatable monthly close: what the diagnostic review must establish before any recurring work is promised, how the cleanup or catch-up project is scoped, sequenced and accepted as a separate paid entry gate, how the chart of accounts, categorization rulebook, feeds, document intake and per-client runbook are standardized so the close runs the same way every month, what the close must reconcile, review, support and disclose before a reporting packet leaves the practice, and which judgment calls must stop at the client's desk or their CPA's instead of being decided by the bookkeeper.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the practice sells a fixed monthly subscription per client tier and this KB governs the delivery side of that subscription: onboarding, the cleanup entry gate, standardization, and the recurring monthly close

the practice performs bookkeeping-side work only; attest, audit, review and compilation engagements, tax return preparation, tax positions and elections, and legal interpretation belong to a licensed professional and are referred out

every cutoff, cadence, threshold, effort estimate and review percentage named here is a mechanism the practice measures and sets for itself, never a market standard, published turnaround norm or benchmark asserted as fact

licensure and title-use rules, records-retention duties, engagement-documentation expectations and data-protection and breach-notification obligations differ by jurisdiction and change over time; this KB names the obligation class and requires current rules to be verified locally with a qualified professional

the practice holds live role-based access to client bank feeds, payment processors, payroll systems and ledgers and receives unfiled source documents, so confidentiality and least-privilege discipline govern every step from the first login onward

the client's ledger lives in a cloud accounting platform fed by bank, card and processor connections plus a document intake channel; specific platforms are examples of a class, and the close must survive any one of them changing behavior
the same small team closes a whole book of clients inside one window each month, so a close step that cannot be repeated for every client in that window is not a real close step
exclusions: designing the fixed-fee monthly tiers and what each tier includes, deriving the subscription fee, selecting and committing to a niche, qualifying prospects, and positioning the offer against hourly bookkeeping or do-it-yourself software - owned by the productized offer and niche selection KB

clients-per-seat capacity math, repricing cadence, the economics of scope creep across the book, retention work, the monthly review conversation with the owner, seasonal and at-risk client handling, ending a mis-fit engagement, and referral engines with CPAs and niche communities - owned by the subscription pricing, capacity and retention KB

attest, audit, review and compilation engagements; tax return preparation; tax positions, elections, deductibility opinions and planning; payroll-tax and sales-tax filing positions; representation before any tax or regulatory authority; and legal interpretation of contracts, entity structure or worker classification
personalized financial, tax, legal, insurance or investment advice to a client; this KB is educational and operational and stops at recording, reconciling, supporting and reporting what happened

invented market rates, benchmark fee tables, published turnaround-time standards, industry error rates or competitor pricing presented as fact; all such figures appear only as mechanisms the practice measures in its own file
step-by-step tutorials for any specific accounting platform's interface, and teaching owners to keep their own books
hiring, training pathways, subcontracting and compensation decisions for the practice's own team
the client's internal operating systems - inventory counts, point-of-sale configuration, project management, collections policy - beyond the data and documents they hand to the ledger

competency_questions.question: How do I handle a correction to a period I already delivered and locked, and what does the client's CPA get from me at year end?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERIOD_LOCK_AND_CORRECTION gives the lock, the materiality-and-filing correction path and the reissue-with-change-note rule, and YEAR_END_CPA_HANDOFF lists the bookkeeping-side package, the authorization requirement and the adjustment intake

glossary.definition: A bounded, paid-or-time-boxed inspection of an incoming client's ledger that establishes what state the books are in - last reconciled date per account, unsupported balances, open-item volume, ledger-to-provider disagreements - and produces a severity-ranked findings register used to scope the cleanup, not to perform it.

The separately scoped, separately agreed remediation of a defined historical period that brings a file from its incoming state to a reconciled, supported starting point; it is the entry gate to the subscription rather than part of the first monthly fee.

The dated trial balance the practice carries forward as the accepted starting point of its own work, together with its source (last filed return, prior accountant's trial balance, or a reconstruction), the differences accepted rather than fixed, and the labelling of anything provided by the client or their CPA as provided-not-verified.

A transaction or balance that cannot be resolved by the practice alone because only the owner knows the fact or only a licensed professional may decide the treatment; it carries a specific question, a default treatment if unanswered, an ask-by date and an aging counter.

A named ledger account where unresolved amounts sit visibly until the client or their CPA answers, used deliberately and reported as a balance with an explanation rather than being buried in a plausible expense account.

Agreeing a ledger account to the source statement or settlement report issued by the bank, card issuer, lender or payment processor, rather than to the platform's feed balance, and explaining every difference item by item instead of forcing an entry to make it balance.

The written, per-client set of coding decisions - recurring vendor to account, transfer versus revenue, principal-and-interest splits, owner-personal handling - each carrying the reason and the source of the decision, from which any automation rule must be derived and against which every close is reviewed.

The set of evidence standing behind every balance-sheet line for a closed period: reconciliation reports, amortization and asset schedules, provider reports, subledger agings, or a written explanation where no document exists.

The monthly deliverable sent to the owner: comparative profit and loss, balance sheet, cash position, a plain-language note page describing what changed and what remains open, and the open-item list, with every figure traceable to the close file.
The software and procedural state that prevents a delivered period from being silently altered, together with the named path by which a genuine correction is made, disclosed and reissued.

nodes.definition: Fix, before a single new client file is opened, what the delivery system actually promises: a named arc that runs from signed engagement through access provisioning, a diagnostic review, a separately agreed cleanup, standardization of the file, and a first supervised close, ending in a steady state where one written checklist produces the same deliverable every month. The charter names the deliverable class of a subscription close - a ledger reconciled to statements, a balance sheet whose every line has support, an owner-readable reporting packet, and a written list of what is still open - and names what the subscription will never contain, such as tax positions, attest work or any opinion reserved to a licensed professional. Above all it defines finished as a checklist state with recorded gate passes rather than a feeling that the month looks about right, and it fixes that onboarding is a project with an end the client passes through, not an open-ended goodwill period in which unpaid catch-up work is quietly absorbed into month one.

included: the stages of the onboarding arc and the gate that ends it
the deliverable class of one subscription close
the written definition of a finished close
the standing refusals that apply to every client
excluded: tier composition and fee derivation, which the offer KB owns
capacity planning and repricing across the book
the monthly review conversation held with the owner after delivery

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: onboarding repeatedly overrunning its gate, or a delivered close that met the checklist and still failed the client, both of which mean the definition of finished is wrong

pros.claim: A written end state turns onboarding from indefinite goodwill into a gated project the client can be held to
pros.example: a client whose three missing bank statements still have not arrived in week six is held at the diagnostic gate rather than being started on a close that cannot reconcile

pros.claim: Defining finished as recorded gate passes makes quality reviewable by someone who did not do the work
pros.example: a reviewer can tell in a minute whether a close is deliverable by checking that each gate has a pass, without re-reading the ledger

cons.claim: One definition of a finished close can be too coarse for an unusual file and then gets applied ceremonially
cons.example: a single-owner consultancy with one bank account being marched through a checklist built for a multi-location restaurant with three processors

cons.claim: A charter written once drifts from what the team actually does unless it is revised when the work changes
cons.example: the charter still describing a paper receipt review two years after the practice moved to a document intake channel

failure_modes: treating onboarding as a courtesy period so cleanup effort is absorbed free into the first monthly fee
calling a close done because the packet was produced when nothing was reconciled
promising close outputs that quietly require licensed judgment the practice cannot give
acceptance_tests: the charter names each stage of the arc, the gate that ends onboarding, the deliverable class of a close, and the standing refusals, all in one document a new team member can read
no close is recorded as done unless every checklist gate carries a recorded pass with a name and a date
revisit_triggers: a new niche or client type needs a close step the charter does not name
onboarding runs past its stated gate for more than one client in a row
a deliverable is promised in a sales conversation that the charter does not contain

nodes.definition: Turn the access a bookkeeper needs into a provisioned, recorded, revocable configuration instead of a pile of credentials collected under time pressure. For each system class the runbook states the least-privilege path: an accountant or team-member role invitation in the ledger sent to a named practice address, a read-only or aggregator-based feed for bank and card accounts, a reporting-level role in the payroll system, read access to the payment processor's settlement reports, and a document channel the client owns and can revoke. It states what is never accepted - the owner's own login, a code relayed by message, a credential in an email thread, a personal file-sharing folder - and what to do when a platform offers only full administrative access: record the limitation, restrict who in the practice holds it, and note the compensating control. Each connection is verified by pulling a known figure through it before the diagnostic starts, entered in an access register with scope, grantor and date, and carried onto a revocation list that is executed when a person leaves the practice or an engagement ends.

included: least-privilege provisioning path per system class
connection verification before work starts
the access register and its revocation list
handling of platforms that offer only full admin access
excluded: the confidentiality rules governing what is done with data once inside, held by the confidentiality node
the practice's own device and endpoint administration
any advice to the client about their own internal access controls

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a platform access-model change, an access near-miss or incident, or a locally verified change in data-protection obligations

pros.claim: Provisioned role-based access survives staff changes and platform password resets without a scramble
pros.example: a departing team member is removed from twelve client ledgers from one register in an afternoon, with nothing left behind in a shared note

pros.claim: Verifying each connection before the diagnostic prevents a whole review being built on partial history
pros.example: pulling last month's closing balance through a new bank connection reveals it only imported ninety days, before anyone reconciles against it

cons.claim: Least-privilege setup is slower than accepting a password and some owners read the refusal as bureaucracy
cons.example: an impatient owner who wanted to hand over one login losing interest halfway through the third role invitation

cons.claim: Read-only or reporting roles sometimes cannot see a report the close needs, forcing a documented exception
cons.example: a payroll reporting role that cannot open the quarterly filing summaries the reconciliation needs, so the client must pull them each period

failure_modes: accepting the owner's credentials to start faster and never unwinding it
leaving a departed team member's access live because no register existed
beginning a diagnostic on a feed that silently imported only part of the history
acceptance_tests: every system the close touches appears in the access register with its role level, who granted it, the date, and the revocation path
no client credential belonging to the owner is stored anywhere in the practice, and any credential the client sent unprompted is recorded as destroyed and replaced with a role invitation
each connection has a verification note showing a known figure was pulled through it before work began
revisit_triggers: a platform changes its role model or retires an accountant-access path
a team member joins or leaves the practice
a connection is re-authenticated or replaced for any reason

nodes.definition: Govern what happens to client financial data once the practice is legitimately inside it, because bookkeeping handles the most sensitive material a small business owns: bank and card activity, payroll registers, customer lists, unfiled documents and the owner's personal spending pattern. The operating rule states who inside the practice may open which client's file and on what device; that data leaves the practice only to a party the client has authorized in writing, only in the form authorized, and only through the agreed channel - the client's CPA, their lender, their new bookkeeper - and never to a referral partner, a peer group, or a social channel; that screenshots, samples and training material are de-identified or synthetic; that a client's affairs are not discussed in shared chats where other clients or staff can read them; and that documents and exports live in practice-controlled storage rather than a personal drive or inbox. It also names data-protection, retention and breach-notification duties as an obligation class that varies by jurisdiction and must be verified locally with a qualified professional rather than assumed from another practice's policy.

included: internal need-to-know rules for who opens which file
the written-authorization test for any outbound disclosure
de-identification of samples and training material
storage discipline and the incident obligation class
excluded: the mechanics of provisioning and revoking access, held by the provisioning runbook
any legal opinion on a jurisdiction's privacy statutes
the client's own obligations to their customers

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an unauthorized disclosure request, a near-miss inside the practice, or locally verified changes to data-protection, retention or notification duties

pros.claim: A written authorization test removes hesitation from the moment a third party asks for the numbers
pros.example: a broker phoning for the client's profit and loss is told the practice needs the client's written instruction, without the bookkeeper improvising a judgment call

pros.claim: Need-to-know file access limits the blast radius of any single compromised account or mistaken send
pros.example: a mis-sent export can only ever contain the one client that team member was working on rather than the whole book

cons.claim: Strict internal partitioning slows cover when someone is ill and another person must pick up the close
cons.example: a second closer waiting for file access to be granted on the morning of a delivery date

cons.claim: Requiring written authorization for every disclosure can read as obstructive to an owner who is standing next to the lender
cons.example: an owner losing patience because a one-line email confirming the request is needed before the packet is forwarded

failure_modes: forwarding a client's statements to their lender or CPA on a verbal request
using a real client's identifiable report as a sales or training sample
discussing a named client's mess in a peer community or a shared practice channel
acceptance_tests: every outbound disclosure of client data in the last period traces to a written client instruction naming the recipient and the material
no sample, screenshot or training artifact in practice use identifies a real client
each team member's file access list matches the clients they are actually assigned to
revisit_triggers: a disclosure request arrives from a party the client has not authorized
a locally verified change in data-protection or retention obligations
a near-miss such as a mis-addressed export or a document left in personal storage

nodes.definition: Keep a standing classification of every request that arrives mid-delivery into bookkeeping-side work the practice performs and licensed-side work it refers, because the questions that cross the line arrive casually, in the middle of a close, from a client who trusts the bookkeeper. Bookkeeping-side means recording what happened, reconciling it to source documents, classifying it according to a rulebook the client and their CPA have seen, producing reports, and describing what the reports show. Licensed-side means deciding whether something is deductible, choosing accrual or cash treatment for tax purposes, setting capitalization thresholds, taking depreciation elections, determining worker classification, deciding sales-tax taxability, signing or preparing returns, any attest or assurance engagement, representation before an authority, and interpreting a contract or entity structure. The node also supplies the sentence the bookkeeper actually says - what the practice can do, what needs their CPA, and the offer to route the question with the client's authorization - and names licensure, title-use and engagement-scope duties as an obligation class whose current rules must be verified in the practice's own jurisdiction rather than copied from a forum answer.

included: the two-column classification of delivery requests
the spoken refusal and referral wording
the obligation-class flag with a verify-locally requirement
how the boundary constrains report notes and packet language
excluded: any statement of what a specific jurisdiction's licensing rules require
the sale-stage version of this boundary, held by the offer KB
choosing which CPA a client should engage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a locally verified change in licensure or title-use rules, a new service line or jurisdiction, or a request class that neither column covers

pros.claim: A prepared classification makes the refusal fast, calm and consistent instead of improvised under client pressure
pros.example: an owner asking mid-call whether a new van should be written off this year gets the same routed answer from whoever is on the call

pros.claim: Routing the question to the CPA rather than dodging it keeps the practice useful while staying inside its lane
pros.example: the bookkeeper drafts the factual summary of the purchase and the CPA returns the treatment, which then becomes a rulebook entry

cons.claim: Clients experience the boundary as unhelpfulness when the answer feels obvious to them
cons.example: an owner irritated that a question they consider simple costs them a separate email to their accountant

cons.claim: The line moves by jurisdiction and by engagement, so the classification needs local verification and periodic review rather than being settled once
cons.example: a practice expanding across a border discovering the title it uses in marketing is restricted there

failure_modes: answering a deductibility or classification question casually because the client asked casually
writing a packet note that recommends a tax or financing action rather than describing what happened
assuming another jurisdiction's rules apply locally instead of verifying them
acceptance_tests: every request class the practice meets in delivery is listed on the bookkeeping side or the licensed side, with the referral wording attached to the licensed side
no delivered packet note or client message contains a recommendation on tax treatment, entity structure, financing or worker classification
the licensing and title-use content names the obligation class and instructs verification with a qualified local professional rather than asserting a rule
revisit_triggers: a request arrives that does not fit either column
the practice takes on a client in a new jurisdiction or a new service line
a client's CPA challenges something the practice decided on its own

nodes.definition: Inspect the incoming ledger inside a fixed box of effort and produce a severity-ranked findings register that tells the practice what the cleanup is, before anyone promises a monthly close. The review walks a standing list: the last reconciled date and unreconciled difference for every bank, card, loan and processor account; balance-sheet accounts carrying balances with no support; the volume sitting in uncategorized, undeposited-funds and clearing accounts; aged receivables and payables full of items that will never settle; payroll totals in the ledger against the payroll provider's own registers; liability accounts for taxes handled elsewhere that never clear; loans without an amortization schedule behind them; owner-personal activity running through business accounts; a second entity's transactions commingled in the same file; duplicate or partial feed history; and any change made to periods that already fed a filed return. Each finding records what it is, why it blocks a reliable close, and the class of work needed to clear it - not the fix itself, because remediation belongs to the scoped cleanup and doing it here is unpaid work that also destroys the evidence of how bad the file was.

included: the standing inspection list and its severity scale
the findings register as the scoping input
the effort box that stops the review turning into free remediation
capture of the file's state before anything is touched
excluded: performing any remediation discovered during the review
judging the tax correctness of prior treatments, which is licensed territory
assessing whether the client is a good commercial fit, which the offer KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cleanups repeatedly uncovering conditions the review missed, or a niche whose files fail in a way the inspection list does not name

pros.claim: A findings register converts a vague bad feeling about the books into a scoped, priceable body of work
pros.example: twenty-two months unreconciled on two accounts plus a payroll ledger that disagrees with the provider becomes three named work classes with severities

pros.claim: Capturing the incoming state protects both sides later when someone asks whether a problem was pre-existing
pros.example: a dated register showing an unsupported loan balance existed before the practice touched the file

cons.claim: A boxed review can miss depth that only appears once reconciliation actually starts
cons.example: a clean-looking card account whose feed turns out to be missing four months of history discovered in the second week of cleanup

cons.claim: Reviewing without fixing frustrates an owner who expected the problem to be solved during the assessment
cons.example: an owner asking why the obvious duplicate deposits were not simply deleted while the reviewer was in there

failure_modes: sliding from reviewing into fixing and giving away the cleanup
reviewing only the profit and loss and missing the balance sheet, where the real damage lives
recording findings without severity so the scope cannot be built from them
acceptance_tests: every balance-sheet account in the incoming file has a status in the register: supported, unsupported, or unknown pending client input
each finding names the work class needed to clear it and its severity, and no remediation was performed during the review
the register is dated and retained as the record of the file's incoming condition
revisit_triggers: cleanup discovers a condition the review did not detect
a new client type shows a failure mode the inspection list does not cover
the review box is consistently overrun for one niche

nodes.definition: Convert the findings register into a project the client agrees to in writing before remediation starts, with a stated historical period, a stated deliverable, an explicit exclusion list, the assumptions the estimate rests on, and a named re-scope trigger for when the file proves worse than the diagnostic showed. The deliverable is described in the same terms the close will later use - accounts reconciled to statements through the agreed period, a supported trial balance at handoff, an open-item list with treatments - so the client can tell when it is finished. The fee is derived as a mechanism the practice measures inside its own file, not a rate taken from anywhere else: countable effort units such as accounts multiplied by months to reconcile, transaction volume bands, missing-document density and the number of entities in the file, priced against the practice's own measured cost to serve and its own uncertainty allowance for a file it has not yet been inside. The contract also states plainly that the monthly subscription cycle does not begin until the gate passes, or begins in a stated limited form, so cleanup effort is never silently financed by the first monthly fee.

included: period, deliverable, exclusions and assumptions of the catch-up project
the measured effort-unit fee mechanism and its uncertainty allowance
the re-scope trigger and how a change is agreed
the relationship between gate passage and the start of the subscription
excluded: the design of the ongoing monthly tiers and their fees, owned by the offer KB
capacity decisions about whether the practice should take the project on
any market rate, benchmark table or competitor comparison

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured overrun or underrun against the effort units on completed cleanups, or a re-scope trigger firing on more than an occasional file

pros.claim: A separate written scope keeps historical remediation from being financed out of a recurring fee designed for steady-state work
pros.example: eighteen months of unreconciled activity is quoted and accepted as its own project rather than disappearing into the first two subscription months

pros.claim: A named re-scope trigger makes the awkward mid-project conversation a contractual step instead of a confrontation
pros.example: discovering a second commingled entity fires the trigger, work pauses, and the change is agreed before more hours are spent

cons.claim: A cleanup quoted from a bounded diagnostic always carries estimation risk that lands on someone
cons.example: a file whose missing-document density only becomes visible in month three of the period being cleaned

cons.claim: Presenting a second invoice before the subscription starts can stall or lose a client who expected one monthly price
cons.example: an owner who agreed to a monthly fee going quiet when the catch-up project is quoted separately

failure_modes: starting remediation on a verbal agreement and arguing about scope afterwards
quoting a cleanup from a copied rate rather than from measured effort units
absorbing discovered extra work silently to avoid an uncomfortable conversation
acceptance_tests: no cleanup work begins before a written scope naming period, deliverable, exclusions, assumptions and re-scope trigger has been accepted
the quoted fee traces to counted effort units and the practice's own cost-to-serve figures, with no external rate cited
the document states when the subscription cycle starts relative to the gate
revisit_triggers: discovery materially contradicts the assumptions the scope rested on
cleanups in one niche consistently overrun the effort units estimated
a client requests work that the exclusion list places outside the project

nodes.definition: Choose one dated trial balance as the point where the practice's own work begins and everything before it is inherited rather than owned. The anchor is taken from the strongest available source in order: the balance sheet underlying the last filed return, the prior accountant's or bookkeeper's closing trial balance, or - where neither exists - a reconstruction built from statements and asset and loan documents. Whatever the source, the anchor memo records the date, the source, the figures accepted without independent verification, the differences found and deliberately not fixed, and the accounts whose balances are labelled provided-not-verified because they came from the client or their CPA. The anchor exists to stop two expensive habits: reconciling forward from balances that later move, and quietly restating periods that already fed a filed return. Anything behind the anchor is touched only with the client's instruction and their CPA in the loop, because a prior filing may depend on the numbers being changed.

included: the anchor date and its source hierarchy
the memo of accepted differences and provided-not-verified labels
the rule governing any change behind the anchor
excluded: deciding whether a prior return should be amended, which is licensed territory
recreating tax basis or depreciation schedules as a tax position
auditing or attesting to the inherited balances

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a corrected trial balance or amended return from the client's CPA, or evidence that lets a provided-not-verified balance finally be supported

pros.claim: A fixed anchor stops the endless backward slide where every unexplained balance invites another month of history
pros.example: an owner asking for two more years back is answered from the memo showing why the anchor sits where the last filed return ended

pros.claim: Labelling inherited balances protects the practice from owning errors it never made
pros.example: an inventory balance carried in as provided-not-verified, flagged in the memo and again in the year-end package

cons.claim: An anchor built on weak inherited numbers embeds an error that surfaces for years as an unexplainable residue
cons.example: an opening equity balance nobody can decompose still needing a note on every balance sheet a year later

cons.claim: Refusing to reach behind the anchor can leave a visibly wrong figure on a report the owner reads monthly
cons.example: a loan showing a balance the lender's statement contradicts because the difference predates the anchor and needs the CPA

failure_modes: reconciling months forward before the starting balances are settled, then redoing them
silently adjusting a period that fed a filed return
accepting inherited balances without recording which ones were never verified
acceptance_tests: the anchor memo names the date, the source, every accepted difference, and every account labelled provided-not-verified
no period behind the anchor has been changed without a recorded client instruction and CPA involvement
the trial balance at the anchor date is retained unchanged as the baseline for all later work
revisit_triggers: the client's CPA supplies a corrected prior trial balance
a filed return is amended and the balances behind the anchor move
reconstruction evidence emerges for an account that was carried in unverified

nodes.definition: Maintain one standard chart of accounts per niche the practice serves, written as reporting lines the owner of that kind of business recognizes, and map every incoming file onto it rather than inheriting whatever the last person built. The standard keeps account count low enough that a monthly report is readable and stable enough that one client's numbers can be discussed against the practice's experience of the niche. A deviation is allowed only when it passes a stated test - the owner actually manages the business by that distinction, or a lender, franchisor or their CPA requires the split - and is denied when it is curiosity, a one-off analysis better done outside the ledger, or historical clutter inherited from a previous bookkeeper. Every mapping decision is recorded from old account to standard line so the cleanup and the first comparative reports can be explained, and new accounts may only be created through this standard, never invented mid-close to make an awkward transaction disappear.

included: the per-niche standard account structure as reporting lines
the deviation test and its allowed reasons
the old-to-standard mapping record
the rule for creating any new account
excluded: tax-driven account requirements or elections, which belong to the client's CPA
the client's internal cost-centre or job-costing design beyond what the ledger carries
software-specific setup instructions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repeated deviation requests of the same shape across a niche, or CPA adjustments that keep landing in accounts the standard does not carry

pros.claim: A niche standard makes every file in the book navigable by anyone in the practice and comparable month to month
pros.example: a closer covering an unfamiliar restaurant file finds food cost, labour and occupancy exactly where the niche standard puts them

pros.claim: A written deviation test turns account requests into a decision with a reason instead of a slow accumulation of one-off accounts
pros.example: a request for a separate account per supplier is declined and answered with a vendor report instead

cons.claim: Standardization can flatten a distinction the owner genuinely runs the business on if the test is applied lazily
cons.example: collapsing two service lines the owner prices separately into one revenue line because the standard only had one

cons.claim: Remapping an existing file breaks the comparability of the client's own historical reports and needs explaining
cons.example: an owner asking why last year's expense categories no longer match this year's report layout

failure_modes: inheriting a previous bookkeeper's account sprawl because remapping felt expensive
creating an account mid-close to park something awkward
approving deviations that nobody can later justify because no reason was recorded
acceptance_tests: every account in the client's live file traces to a standard line or to a recorded deviation with its reason and approver
the old-to-standard mapping is retained so any historical figure can be explained
no account was created during a close without going through the standard
revisit_triggers: the niche standard cannot express something several clients in that niche genuinely manage by
a client's CPA or lender requires a reporting split the standard lacks
account count in a file grows past what the monthly report can carry

nodes.definition: Run remediation in a fixed order chosen so that no pass invalidates an earlier one. Connections and history are verified first, then the anchor is confirmed, then accounts are mapped onto the standard, and only then does month-by-month work begin: cash and card accounts reconciled to statements chronologically forward, never newest month first; duplicated or partially imported feed activity removed as it is met; payment processor settlements agreed to the processor's own reports so that gross revenue, fees and refunds separate correctly; payroll agreed to the provider's registers; receivables and payables aged and stale items dispositioned; and loans, owner accounts and equity handled last because they are the accounts most often used as a dumping ground and only make sense once everything else has landed. Categorization follows reconciliation within each month rather than preceding it, because recoding after a reconciliation break is the single most common piece of avoidable rework in a catch-up project.

included: the ordered passes of a catch-up project
the chronological-forward and reconcile-before-categorize rules
where processor, payroll and loan work sits in the order
handling of duplicate and partial feed history
excluded: deciding the tax treatment of anything discovered, which routes to the CPA
the fee and scope of the project itself
the recurring monthly close, which starts only after the gate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured rework inside cleanup projects, especially months touched more than once, or a niche whose processor and payroll structure needs a different order

pros.claim: A fixed order makes a large catch-up predictable enough to staff, pause and resume without loss
pros.example: a project handed to a second person mid-way resumes at the next unreconciled month rather than starting over

pros.claim: Reconciling before coding removes the rework loop where categories are redone after a missing deposit appears
pros.example: four months of coding avoided being touched twice once a duplicated card feed was found during reconciliation

cons.claim: Strict chronological order delays the recent months the owner actually cares about seeing
cons.example: an owner waiting through eleven older months before the current quarter's numbers become meaningful

cons.claim: Leaving owner and loan accounts to the end concentrates the hardest judgment calls into the final pass, often against a deadline
cons.example: a pile of owner transfers all needing client answers surfacing in the last week of the project

failure_modes: starting with the most recent month because it feels most useful, then redoing it when earlier balances move
categorizing a month before its bank account reconciles
clearing a suspense balance with a plug entry to make a month close
acceptance_tests: each month in the cleanup period shows a completed reconciliation before any categorization review of that month is recorded
reconciliation reports exist per account per month across the agreed period, in date order with no gaps
no balancing entry without a documented explanation appears in the cleanup period
revisit_triggers: a pass has to be redone because an earlier one moved
feed history is discovered to be incomplete after reconciliation began
the project is paused, restaffed or resumed after a break

nodes.definition: Give every client one visible channel through which statements, bills, receipts, loan documents and payroll reports reach the practice, and a register of what is missing for each period so chasing is a list rather than a memory. The channel is practice-controlled or client-owned storage the practice is invited into - never a personal messaging app, never the bookkeeper's own inbox or personal drive - so that documents are retained, retrievable and covered by the confidentiality rule. Missing items are chased on a stated cadence with escalating channels and a stop rule that hands the decision back to the client rather than letting an item be chased forever, and each unresolved document becomes an open item with a default treatment. Retention periods and the format in which documents must be kept are named as an obligation class that differs by jurisdiction and client type and must be verified locally rather than assumed from habit.

included: the single intake channel and its storage rules
the missing-document register per period
the chasing cadence, escalation and stop rule
retention named as an obligation class to verify locally
excluded: deciding whether a document substantiates a deduction, which is licensed territory
designing the client's internal filing or approval workflow
the open-item queue mechanics themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: rising missing-document counts per period, or a locally verified change in retention obligations

pros.claim: One channel makes missing documents countable, which makes chasing a scheduled task instead of nagging
pros.example: the register shows three card statements outstanding for the period, chased together in one message rather than three separate asks

pros.claim: Practice-controlled storage keeps source documents retrievable when a lender, the CPA or the client asks a year later
pros.example: producing the loan agreement behind an amortization schedule during the year-end package without contacting the client

cons.claim: Owners route documents through whatever is convenient, so a single channel needs constant re-teaching
cons.example: receipts photographed and texted to the bookkeeper's phone the week after the channel was set up

cons.claim: Collecting and storing more documents increases the practice's own retention and protection burden
cons.example: a growing archive of client bank statements that must be stored, controlled and eventually disposed of under a locally verified rule

failure_modes: accepting documents through personal channels so they are never retained or retrievable
chasing the same item every month with no stop rule and no default treatment
closing a period without recording which documents were never received
acceptance_tests: every period has a missing-document register showing what was requested, when, and what was received
no source document for the period sits outside practice-controlled or client-owned agreed storage
each document never received has a default treatment recorded and disclosed in the packet
revisit_triggers: a client persistently bypasses the intake channel
a locally verified change in retention or document-format obligations
the missing-document register grows across consecutive periods

nodes.definition: Treat every automated connection into the ledger as a component that fails quietly and check it deliberately rather than trusting that data arrived. The known failure shapes are specific: an authorization that expires so transactions simply stop; a reconnection that re-imports weeks of activity as duplicates; a connection that back-fills only part of the history; a renamed or re-numbered account that starts landing in the wrong ledger account; a commerce or point-of-sale integration that posts summary journals whose totals cannot be traced to individual settlements; and a processor whose deposits arrive net of fees, refunds and chargebacks so revenue is understated until the settlement report is used. The pre-close check compares, for every connected account, the last imported transaction date and the feed balance against the statement or settlement report, and any break goes into a register and is repaired - with missing history imported from statements rather than assumed - before categorization of that period begins.

included: the catalogue of known connection failure shapes
the pre-close feed and integration check
the break register and the repair-before-coding rule
netting behaviour of processor deposits as a data issue
excluded: choosing or recommending accounting software or integrations for the client
the client's own commerce platform configuration
the reconciliation itself, which uses the repaired data

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a platform changing connection or settlement behaviour, or post-close discovery of duplicated or missing feed activity

pros.claim: A pre-close check catches silent breaks while there is still time to fix them inside the window
pros.example: an expired card connection found on the first close day instead of during a failed reconciliation on the delivery day

pros.claim: Knowing the failure shapes converts a mysterious mismatch into a named, quickly diagnosed condition
pros.example: a sudden pile of duplicate transactions immediately read as a reconnection re-import rather than investigated from scratch

cons.claim: Checking every connection for every client each month is real recurring effort that the subscription must carry
cons.example: a client with two banks, three cards, two processors and a payroll integration needing eight checks before coding starts

cons.claim: Feed behaviour changes outside the practice's control, so the catalogue is always slightly behind reality
cons.example: a platform changing how refunds are posted mid-year with no notice, discovered through a reconciliation difference

failure_modes: reconciling to the feed balance and inheriting the feed's own error
deleting apparent duplicates that were genuine repeat transactions
treating processor net deposits as revenue and understating both revenue and fees
acceptance_tests: each connected account has a pre-close check recorded for the period showing last transaction date and balance compared to the statement or settlement report
every break in the register has a repair note, and any imported history is traced to a statement rather than estimated
no categorization of a period begins while an unrepaired break for that period is open
revisit_triggers: a platform changes connection, refund or settlement behaviour
duplicate or missing transactions are found after a period was closed
a new integration is added to a client's file

nodes.definition: Write down, per client, how recurring things are coded and why, so that coding is a rule being applied rather than a judgment being re-made every month by whoever has the file open. The rulebook carries the recurring vendor to account mapping with its reason; the treatment of transfers between the client's own accounts so they never appear as revenue or expense; loan payments split into principal and interest from the amortization schedule rather than estimated; owner-personal spending routed to the owner account rather than buried in a plausible expense line; deposits distinguished between revenue, transfers, owner contributions, refunds and loan proceeds; and payments to individuals recorded according to the classification the client or their CPA has determined, which the bookkeeper records but never decides. Every automation rule inside the platform must derive from a rulebook entry, be reviewed on a stated cadence, and never auto-post a class the rulebook marks ambiguous - because a wrong automated rule silently multiplies itself across every month until someone reads the report carefully.

included: per-client coding rules with reasons and sources
handling of transfers, owner activity, loan splits and deposit types
automation rules derived from and reviewed against the rulebook
the marking of ambiguous classes that must never auto-post
excluded: determining deductibility, worker classification or taxability, which are recorded from the client or their CPA, never decided here
the niche account structure itself
the review pass that tests the rulebook each month

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: review-pass findings that trace to a rulebook entry, a CPA reversing a recorded treatment, or a change in the client's operations

pros.claim: A written rule asked once and reused stops the same question being sent to the owner every month
pros.example: a recurring supplier settled the first month and never queried again, with the reason on record for the next closer

pros.claim: Recording the source of each decision makes the file defensible when the CPA or the owner asks why something sits where it does
pros.example: pointing to the CPA's own written answer behind a capitalized purchase during the year-end review

cons.claim: Rules calcify: a mapping that was right when written keeps applying after the client's business changes
cons.example: a vendor still coded as marketing long after the client began buying inventory from them

cons.claim: Automation built on the rulebook spreads any error at speed and hides it behind apparent tidiness
cons.example: a mis-set rule coding every deposit from one customer as a transfer, quietly understating revenue for months

failure_modes: coding from memory instead of the rulebook so two closers treat the same vendor differently
letting automation post an ambiguous class without review
recording a treatment the bookkeeper decided in territory reserved to the client's CPA
acceptance_tests: every recurring vendor and every non-obvious transaction class in the client's file has a rulebook entry with a reason and the source of the decision
every active automation rule maps to a rulebook entry and has been reviewed within the stated cadence
no rulebook entry records a determination the practice made in licensed territory
revisit_triggers: the client changes what they buy, sell or how they pay for it
the review pass finds the same rule producing wrong results
the CPA overturns a treatment the rulebook carried

nodes.definition: Hold everything the practice cannot resolve alone in one visible queue instead of leaving it scattered through the ledger or in a mailbox. An entry carries the transaction reference and amount, the question phrased in the owner's language rather than in accounting terms, the default treatment that will be applied if no answer arrives, an ask-by date tied to the close calendar, and an aging counter that survives across periods. Questions are batched and sent on a stated cadence so the owner receives one considered list rather than a drip of interruptions they learn to ignore, and unanswered items are posted to a named holding account where the balance stays visible and is disclosed in the packet rather than being coded to a plausible expense to make the queue disappear. A carry limit says how much unresolved value or how many aged items a close can carry before the file stops being closeable, which turns a slow-motion problem into a decision the practice and the client take deliberately.

included: the queue entry structure with default treatment and ask-by date
batching cadence for client questions
the named holding account and its disclosure
the carry limit that stops an unclosable file being closed anyway
excluded: the commercial response to a chronically unresponsive client, owned by the retention KB
deciding treatments that require the client's CPA, which routing handles
chasing source documents, held by the intake system

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: queue aging and default-treatment reversal rates measured across closes, or repeated entries of one class that a rulebook entry should have absorbed

pros.claim: Batched questions with defaults get answered because the owner can clear them in one sitting and knows what happens if they do not
pros.example: eleven items sent as one list with proposed treatments, of which the owner corrects two and approves the rest in a single reply

pros.claim: A visible holding balance keeps unresolved money honest instead of hiding it inside an expense line
pros.example: an unexplained transfer sitting in the holding account and appearing on the packet rather than being coded as supplies

cons.claim: Default treatments can become the answer by attrition when a client never engages with the list
cons.example: a series of unexplained card purchases defaulting to the owner account month after month because nobody replies

cons.claim: Batching delays resolution of an item that could have been settled with one quick message on the day it appeared
cons.example: a large deposit that the owner would have explained instantly waiting a week for the scheduled question list

failure_modes: coding an unknown item to a plausible account to keep the queue short
asking the owner in scattered messages until they stop reading them
carrying an aged queue into another close because nobody applied the limit
acceptance_tests: every open item carries a question in owner language, a default treatment, an ask-by date and an aging count
the holding account balance at close equals the sum of unresolved items and is disclosed in the packet
no close is delivered with the queue above the carry limit without a recorded decision by the practice and the client
revisit_triggers: the queue ages past the carry limit for two consecutive periods
the same class of item keeps entering the queue, which means the rulebook has a gap
a default treatment is later overturned by the client or their CPA

nodes.definition: Keep one document per client that lets any qualified person in the practice run that client's close without asking the person who normally does it. It records the systems and the access path into each, the connections and their known quirks, the approved chart-of-accounts deviations and the reason for each, the rulebook exceptions, the close calendar dates agreed with this client, who answers questions and how quickly they usually do, what the reporting packet contains for them, and the landmines learned the hard way - the account the owner uses personally, the integration that posts summaries, the month their seasonal activity distorts everything. Its second purpose is to make customization visible: anything in the runbook that departs from the practice standard is work that is being done specially for this client, recorded where it can be seen, counted and reconsidered rather than living silently in one person's head where it disappears when they are ill or leave.

included: systems, access paths and connection quirks per client
approved deviations and exceptions with reasons
the agreed calendar, contacts and packet composition
known landmines and seasonal distortions
excluded: stored credentials of any kind, which the provisioning rule forbids
capacity or pricing consequences of the recorded customization, owned by the pricing KB
the client's own internal procedures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cover or hand-off that required contacting the usual closer, or a close failure traced to information that existed only in someone's memory

pros.claim: A written runbook makes cover and hand-off possible without quality collapsing
pros.example: a second closer delivering an unfamiliar file on time because the runbook named the integration that posts summary journals

pros.claim: Recording every deviation makes silent customization visible before it becomes uncosted standing work
pros.example: three custom reports listed in one client's runbook prompting a conversation the practice would otherwise never have had

cons.claim: A runbook that is not updated as the file changes is worse than none because it is trusted
cons.example: a closer following a documented feed path that was replaced two months earlier and losing an hour

cons.claim: Maintaining a runbook for every client is standing overhead that produces no client-visible output
cons.example: an afternoon each quarter spent updating runbooks that no client will ever thank the practice for

failure_modes: keeping the file's real quirks in one person's head
letting the runbook drift until nobody trusts it
recording credentials or access secrets in it
acceptance_tests: a qualified person who has never seen the file can run the close from the runbook without contacting the usual closer
every deviation and exception in the file appears in the runbook with a reason and a date
the runbook contains no credential, security answer or access secret
revisit_triggers: the client changes systems, banks, processors or personnel
a closer needed information that was not in the runbook
a deviation is approved, retired or found to be unused

nodes.definition: End the catch-up project with an acceptance artifact rather than a quiet drift into monthly work, because the boundary between remediation and subscription is exactly where disputes and unpaid effort accumulate. The pack contains reconciliation reports per account for the cleaned period, the trial balance at the handoff date, the list of items that remain unresolved with the treatment applied to each, the assumptions that were accepted, and a plain statement of what was deliberately not done - no tax positions taken, no attest work performed, nothing behind the anchor restated. The client acknowledges it in writing; where the client's CPA needs to see it, it is sent only on the client's written authorization and framed as bookkeeping-side output for their review rather than as a finished tax-ready product. Only when the acknowledgement is recorded does the recurring close calendar start, and the first close after the gate is run with an explicit second look because it is the period most likely to inherit an unnoticed cleanup residue.

included: the contents of the cleanup acceptance pack
the written acknowledgement and the authorization for any CPA copy
the statement of what was not done
the trigger that starts the recurring calendar
excluded: the commercial handling of a client who refuses to acknowledge, owned by the retention KB
any assurance or opinion on the cleaned figures
the fee for the project, fixed in the scope contract

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: residues found in the first closes after gates, or disputes about what a cleanup included

pros.claim: A written acceptance fixes the moment the practice's ongoing responsibility begins and the inherited past ends
pros.example: a question about a two-year-old transaction answered from the pack's statement of what was inherited rather than fixed

pros.claim: Stating the limitations at handoff prevents the pack from being read as tax-ready or assured work
pros.example: a CPA receiving the pack with the limitation page attached and knowing exactly what review it still needs

cons.claim: Clients often will not read or return an acknowledgement, which stalls the start of the cycle
cons.example: an owner who considers the work obviously finished never replying to the acceptance request

cons.claim: A hard gate can hold up a client who urgently needs current reporting while formalities complete
cons.example: a lender deadline arriving while the acceptance pack sits unacknowledged

failure_modes: sliding from cleanup into monthly work with no marker, so both scopes blur
sending the pack to the client's CPA without written authorization
presenting the cleaned period as tax-ready or assured
acceptance_tests: the acceptance pack contains reconciliation reports, the handoff trial balance, unresolved items with treatments, accepted assumptions and the statement of what was not done
the client's acknowledgement is recorded with a date before the first subscription close is started
any copy sent to a third party traces to a written client authorization
revisit_triggers: the first close after the gate uncovers a cleanup residue
a client disputes what the cleanup covered
the acknowledgement is refused or goes unanswered past the stated period

nodes.definition: Publish, per client, the input cutoff, the internal close window and the delivery date, expressed as offsets from period end that the practice has measured on its own work rather than promises borrowed from someone else's marketing. The calendar exists because a book of clients cannot all be closed on the same day: clients are staggered across the window by their input dependencies - those whose statements arrive early, those whose payroll lands late, those with processors that settle on a lag - so the team's real working days carry the whole book. It also fixes one written rule for a missed cutoff instead of a case-by-case negotiation each month: either the close proceeds on schedule with the gap disclosed in the packet and the item carried as an open item, or the delivery moves by a stated amount, with the choice made once per client and recorded in the runbook rather than argued in the moment.

included: per-client cutoff, close window and delivery date as measured offsets
staggering the book across the window by input dependency
the single written rule for a missed cutoff
excluded: how many clients one closer can carry, owned by the pricing and capacity KB
any published industry turnaround standard
the content of the packet delivered on the date

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured close durations and missed-date counts across the book, or a change in a client's input timing

pros.claim: A published cutoff converts chasing into a schedule the client can meet and the team can staff
pros.example: a client whose card statements always arrive late is placed in the second half of the window instead of being chased on day two

pros.claim: One written missed-cutoff rule removes a monthly negotiation and makes late delivery a client-visible consequence
pros.example: the packet arriving on time with a disclosed gap because the rule for this client says the date does not move

cons.claim: Staggering by dependency makes the schedule fragile: one client moving disturbs the sequence behind them
cons.example: a payroll integration failing for one client and pushing three other files into the same afternoon

cons.claim: A firm delivery date can force a close with a disclosed gap that the owner would rather have waited for
cons.example: delivering without the final processor settlement because the rule said the date holds

failure_modes: promising a delivery date the practice has never measured itself against
renegotiating the cutoff every month so it stops meaning anything
closing over a missing input without disclosing the gap
acceptance_tests: each client's cutoff, close window and delivery date are published to them and recorded in the runbook
the offsets used trace to the practice's own measured close durations rather than an external standard
every close delivered with an unmet input shows the disclosed gap and the applied missed-cutoff rule
revisit_triggers: delivery dates are missed for the same client repeatedly
a client's input pattern changes, for example a new payroll provider or processor
the book grows or restaffs so the window no longer fits the working days

nodes.definition: Reconcile every bank, card, loan and payment processor account to the source document the third party issued - the statement, the lender's balance, the settlement report - and never to the platform's own feed balance, because reconciling to the feed only proves the ledger agrees with itself. Each difference is explained item by item: outstanding payments and deposits are listed and aged, timing items are identified as timing, and anything that cannot be explained stays visible. Processor accounts are reconciled against settlement reports so that gross sales, fees, refunds and chargebacks land separately instead of arriving as a single net deposit. The two rules that give this node its weight are that a forced entry made to bring a reconciliation into agreement is a recorded defect rather than a fix, and that an unexplained difference blocks the affected statement from being delivered - because the reconciliation is the only step in the whole close that independently proves the ledger against the outside world.

included: statement and settlement-report based reconciliation of every cash and liability account
item-by-item explanation and aging of differences
the no-forced-entry rule and the blocking rule
processor gross-versus-net separation
excluded: whether a reconciled transaction is deductible or taxable, which is licensed territory
reconciling the client's own internal subsystems to each other
the support assembly for non-cash balance-sheet accounts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recurring differences in a specific account, a statement or settlement format change, or post-delivery defects traced to reconciliation

pros.claim: Statement-based reconciliation is the one control that catches missing, duplicated and fabricated activity at once
pros.example: a duplicated supplier payment from a reconnected feed found because the statement shows one payment, not two

pros.claim: Aging outstanding items surfaces stale entries that would otherwise sit in the ledger indefinitely
pros.example: a cheque outstanding for many months prompting a client question rather than quietly propping up the balance

cons.claim: Full statement reconciliation of every account every month is the heaviest recurring cost in the close
cons.example: a client with several cards and two processors where reconciliation consumes most of the file's close time

cons.claim: The blocking rule creates real conflict with the delivery date when a difference resists explanation
cons.example: an unexplained processor difference on the delivery morning forcing the affected statement to be held

failure_modes: ticking a reconciliation as complete against the feed balance rather than the statement
posting a balancing entry to clear a stubborn difference
treating net processor deposits as revenue so fees and refunds never appear
acceptance_tests: every cash, card, loan and processor account has a reconciliation report for the period referencing the third-party document it was agreed to
no unexplained difference and no undocumented balancing entry exists in any reconciled account at delivery
processor accounts show gross sales, fees, refunds and chargebacks separately, traced to the settlement report
revisit_triggers: a difference recurs in the same account across periods
a bank, lender or processor changes statement format or settlement timing
a post-delivery defect traces back to a reconciliation

nodes.definition: Run a deliberate review of the coded period rather than a second pass of coding, on the assumption that the first pass and the automation were both partly wrong. The review compares the period against the prior period and against the rulebook and looks for a specific list: accounts whose balance moved materially against their own history without a known cause, vendors appearing for the first time, transactions posted by automation in classes the rulebook marks reviewable, anything still uncategorized, candidates for owner-personal spending, round-number and duplicate patterns, negative balances where none can exist, revenue that moved without a matching change in deposits, and expenses in months where the underlying activity did not occur. What the reviewer cannot resolve becomes an open item with a question for the owner; what is ambiguous by class goes to routing rather than being decided; and anything the review keeps catching in the same shape is a rulebook gap to be closed rather than a monthly chore to be repeated.

included: the comparative and anomaly scan list
review of automation-posted classes
conversion of unresolved findings into open items or routed questions
feeding recurring findings back into the rulebook
excluded: deciding treatments reserved to the client or their CPA
re-performing the reconciliation
interpreting business performance for the owner, which the packet describes and the review conversation owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-delivery defects that the scan list should have caught, or repeated flags of one shape that point at a rulebook gap

pros.claim: Comparative review catches the errors that individually look plausible and only stand out against history
pros.example: an expense line double its usual level because a recurring supplier was coded to two different accounts by two closers

pros.claim: Reviewing automation output keeps rule-driven speed from silently propagating a wrong mapping
pros.example: a rule that started coding a customer's payments as transfers caught in the first month rather than the fourth

cons.claim: Comparative scanning is weak in files with genuinely irregular activity, where everything looks anomalous
cons.example: a project-based trades client whose revenue and material costs swing so widely that variance flags stop being informative

cons.claim: The review can slide into re-coding by preference, undoing another closer's rulebook-compliant work
cons.example: a reviewer recoding a vendor because they would have chosen a different account, without changing the rulebook

failure_modes: treating the review as a second coding pass instead of a test of the rules
clearing anomaly flags without an explanation recorded
deciding an ambiguous treatment during review instead of routing it
acceptance_tests: every item on the scan list is executed for the period, with each flag either explained, converted to an open item, or routed
no transaction remains uncategorized at delivery outside the named holding account
any change made during review that departs from the rulebook is accompanied by a rulebook update
revisit_triggers: the same anomaly class recurs across periods or clients
a defect found after delivery would have been visible on the scan list
automation coverage in a file changes materially

nodes.definition: Apply a standing three-way rule to every question that will not resolve itself, because most damage in a bookkeeping practice comes from a well-meaning person answering a question that was not theirs to answer. The bookkeeper decides only what the rulebook already covers, applying a recorded decision rather than forming a new one. The client decides facts only they hold: what a payment was for, which job or property it belongs to, whether a purchase was personal, whether a deposit was a loan from them or revenue. The client's CPA decides treatment: deductibility, capitalize-or-expense thresholds, depreciation, accrual policy adopted for tax purposes, worker classification, sales-tax taxability, and anything touching a filed or upcoming return. Every routed question is logged with who was asked, when, what they answered and in what form, the answer is recorded as a rulebook entry so it is never asked twice, and any approach to the CPA happens with the client's authorization and with the client copied, never as a private arrangement around the person who owns the data.

included: the three-way decision rule and worked examples of each lane
the routing log and its conversion into rulebook entries
the authorization and copy rule for approaching the CPA
the fallback treatment when no answer arrives in time
excluded: forming the licensed opinion itself
choosing or evaluating the client's CPA
the sales-stage version of the boundary conversation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reversals of default treatments, questions that fit no lane, or a CPA challenging a determination the practice recorded

pros.claim: Explicit lanes keep the practice useful and safe at once: it moves the question rather than guessing or refusing flatly
pros.example: a vehicle purchase summarized factually, sent to the CPA with the client copied, and returned as a treatment the rulebook then carries

pros.claim: Logging answers turns one awkward question into permanent practice knowledge
pros.example: the CPA's capitalization threshold answer applied automatically to the next three asset purchases without re-asking

cons.claim: Routing costs elapsed time and the close may have to proceed without the answer
cons.example: a CPA on extension deadlines not replying before the delivery date, forcing the default treatment and a disclosure

cons.claim: Clients sometimes read routing as the bookkeeper avoiding work or lacking competence
cons.example: an owner asking why they pay a bookkeeper if a simple depreciation question goes to their accountant

failure_modes: answering a licensed-side question because the client pressed and the answer seemed obvious
contacting the client's CPA without authorization or without copying the client
receiving an answer and never converting it into a standing rule, so it is asked again next month
acceptance_tests: every routed question has a log entry naming the lane, the person asked, the date, the answer and its form
no licensed-side determination in the file was made by the practice itself
each received answer appears as a rulebook entry before the next close of that file
revisit_triggers: a question arrives that does not sit cleanly in any lane
a default treatment applied for lack of an answer is later reversed
the same routed question recurs, meaning the rulebook entry was never written

nodes.definition: Require that every balance-sheet line in a closed period resolves to something a third party could inspect: a reconciliation report, an amortization schedule for each loan, a fixed-asset additions and disposals list, a prepaid or deferred schedule following the policy the client's CPA set, a provider report for payroll liabilities, a subledger aging for receivables and payables, a statement for cash, or - where no document exists - a written explanation naming what the balance is and why it is there. Alongside the support requirement runs a standing scan for the residues that betray a weak close: negative balances in asset or liability accounts that cannot go negative, holding and clearing accounts that never empty, opening-balance-equity residue left from a conversion, payroll liabilities that do not agree to the provider's own reports, agings that do not tie to their control account, and inter-entity or owner-loan accounts drifting with no documented basis. The profit and loss gets the attention in the client conversation, but the balance sheet is where an unreliable close actually shows.

included: the support requirement per balance-sheet account class
the residue and impossibility scan list
written explanations where no document exists
the rule that nothing unsupported leaves in a packet
excluded: setting the capitalization, prepaid or accrual policies themselves, which the client's CPA owns
valuation opinions on any asset
assurance or attestation of the balances

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: year-end adjustments landing on balance-sheet accounts the support file claimed were supported, or residues surfacing after delivery

pros.claim: Named support turns the balance sheet from a plausible-looking report into something defensible to a CPA or a lender
pros.example: a year-end request for the basis of a liability answered from the support file in minutes rather than reconstructed

pros.claim: The residue scan catches the failures that reconciliation alone will never reveal
pros.example: a clearing account quietly accumulating unmatched amounts across months while every bank account reconciles perfectly

cons.claim: Assembling support for every line each month is heavy for small files where most balances barely move
cons.example: rebuilding the same three schedules monthly for a one-person consultancy whose balance sheet is nearly static

cons.claim: Written explanations can become a permanent substitute for finding the real support
cons.example: an inherited balance carrying the same explanatory note every month for a year with nobody resolving it

failure_modes: delivering a balance sheet nobody has actually looked at line by line
leaving negative or impossible balances because the profit and loss looked right
letting holding, clearing and opening-equity balances persist indefinitely
acceptance_tests: every balance-sheet account for the period has named support attached or a written explanation recorded
the residue scan is executed and every flagged balance is either cleared or explained and disclosed
payroll liability and subledger agings agree to the provider report and control accounts respectively
revisit_triggers: a balance carries the same written explanation across several periods
the client's CPA changes a policy the schedules depend on
a residue is found after delivery

nodes.definition: Assemble the monthly deliverable so that an owner who is not an accountant can read it and a professional who is can trace it. The packet carries a comparative profit and loss, the balance sheet, the cash position, and a short note page written in plain language that states what changed and why in factual terms, what remains open with the treatment applied, what was assumed, and what needs a decision from the owner or their CPA. Every figure must trace back to the close file, so nothing appears in the packet that the support file cannot stand behind. The line the note page must not cross is the difference between describing and advising: it may say that a supplier cost rose, that a liability was paid down, that an unexplained transfer sits in the holding account awaiting explanation; it may not recommend a tax treatment, an entity change, a financing move or a pricing decision. Anything closed with a gap - a missing statement, an unanswered question, a default treatment - is disclosed in the packet rather than smoothed over, because the packet is the client's only view of how solid the month actually is.

included: packet composition and comparative presentation
plain-language factual note discipline
traceability of every figure to the close file
disclosure of gaps, assumptions and default treatments
excluded: the monthly review conversation and its retention role, owned by the pricing and retention KB
recommendations on tax, financing, entity or pricing decisions
forecasting or valuation work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: client questions that reveal the packet did not communicate, or a note found to have crossed from description into recommendation

pros.claim: A factual note page makes the numbers usable to an owner who would otherwise only see two statements they do not read
pros.example: a note explaining that a large expense was an annual insurance payment rather than a cost increase, in one sentence

pros.claim: Disclosing gaps in the packet keeps trust intact when a client later discovers a month was closed with something missing
pros.example: an owner who already knew from the note that one card statement was outstanding when the figures were produced

cons.claim: Plain language is one short step from advice, and an offhand sentence can cross the licensed boundary
cons.example: a note suggesting the owner might want to prepay next year's expenses, which is a tax recommendation

cons.claim: Notes take real time each month and owners vary hugely in whether they read them
cons.example: a carefully written note page for a client who only ever opens the cash figure

failure_modes: delivering statements with no notes so the owner cannot tell a real change from an artifact
writing a recommendation into the notes and crossing into licensed territory
presenting a month closed with gaps as if it were complete
acceptance_tests: every figure in the packet traces to the close file and its support
the note page contains only factual description, with no recommendation on tax, entity, financing or pricing
every gap, assumption and default treatment applied during the close appears in the packet
revisit_triggers: a client repeatedly misreads a section of the packet
a note is found to have crossed into recommendation
a gap was discovered by the client that the packet did not disclose

nodes.definition: Require a named sign-off before anything is delivered and treat every defect found afterwards as data rather than embarrassment.
