The sign-off is performed by someone other than the preparer where the practice has more than one person, and in a solo practice by the same person working on a different day strictly against the written checklist rather than from memory: checklist complete, reconciliations attached, balance-sheet support present, open items disclosed, packet figures traced, notes inside the boundary. The record names who signed, on what date, and against which checklist version. Every defect found after delivery - by the client reading the packet, by the reviewer in the next period, by the CPA at year end - is logged with its cause class: rulebook gap, feed or integration break, missing document, standard chart-of-accounts gap, calendar or capacity pressure, or human slip. Cause classes drive the fix: a rulebook gap changes the rulebook, a recurring feed break changes the pre-close check, and a pattern of slips under deadline is a scheduling problem, not a training problem.

included: the independent or separated sign-off and its record
the delivery checklist as the sign-off basis
the defect log with cause classification
the routing of each cause class to the artifact it should change
excluded: performance management of individuals
the client-facing apology or commercial remedy, owned by the retention KB
re-opening a locked period, which the correction node governs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect counts by cause class over time, and whether defects reaching clients fall after each system change

pros.claim: A second pair of eyes against a checklist catches what the preparer's own assumptions made invisible
pros.example: a reviewer noticing an entire missing payroll run that the preparer had mentally accounted for and never checked

pros.claim: Cause classification turns scattered mistakes into a short list of system changes
pros.example: three defects in one quarter all classed as feed breaks, producing one change to the pre-close check rather than three apologies

cons.claim: A solo practice cannot achieve true independence, and separation by time is a weaker control
cons.example: the same person reviewing their own close two days later and reading what they expected to see

cons.claim: Sign-off consumes window time exactly when the window is tightest
cons.example: a review queue backing up on the last two delivery days of the month across the whole book

failure_modes: signing off by habit without executing the checklist
fixing defects silently so the pattern never becomes visible
classing every defect as human error, which prevents any system change
acceptance_tests: each delivered close carries a sign-off record naming the reviewer, the date and the checklist version
every defect found after delivery has a log entry with a cause class and the artifact it changed
no cause class is used without a linked change or an explicit decision not to change anything
revisit_triggers: the same cause class appears repeatedly across clients or periods
a defect reaches the client rather than being caught at sign-off
the checklist is changed, which resets what sign-off means

nodes.definition: Lock each period once it has been signed off and delivered so the software cannot silently change numbers the client has already seen, and define in advance the only path by which a genuine correction is made. The path turns on two questions: whether the item is material to the client's decisions and reporting, and whether the period fed a filed return or a submitted lender or grant report. Immaterial items are corrected in the current open period with a note in the next packet. Material items, and anything touching a period behind a filing, go to the client and their CPA before anything is reopened, because the correction may have consequences the practice is not licensed to weigh. Every change to a locked period is recorded with who authorized it, when, what changed and why, and a corrected packet is reissued with a change note rather than the original being quietly replaced - a client discovering that a delivered figure changed without explanation loses more trust than the original error ever cost.

included: the lock applied at delivery
the materiality and filing test that selects the correction path
the authorization and audit record for any reopening
reissue with a change note
excluded: deciding whether a return should be amended, which belongs to the client's CPA
the practice's commercial response to a costly error
restating periods behind the opening anchor, governed by the anchor rule

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the frequency and materiality of reopenings, or a CPA amending a return that covers a locked period

pros.claim: A lock makes delivered numbers stable enough that reports, comparisons and conversations can be trusted
pros.example: a comparative report matching the packet the owner received six months ago rather than a quietly shifted version

pros.claim: A prepared correction path stops each error becoming an improvised decision under embarrassment
pros.example: a coding error found in a period behind a filed return going straight to the client and their CPA rather than being fixed quietly

cons.claim: Corrections in the current period rather than at source distort the month in which they land and need explaining
cons.example: a prior-period expense appearing in this month's profit and loss with a note that the comparative is affected

cons.claim: The materiality test needs judgment the practice must apply consistently, and clients differ on what matters to them
cons.example: an amount irrelevant to one client being decision-relevant to another with tight lender covenants

failure_modes: leaving periods unlocked so delivered figures drift silently
reopening a filed period without the client and their CPA
replacing a delivered packet without a change note
acceptance_tests: every delivered period is locked and any change to it carries an authorization record with who, when, what and why
no period that fed a filed return was reopened without recorded client and CPA involvement
each corrected figure previously delivered was reissued with a change note rather than silently replaced
revisit_triggers: a locked period needs reopening
the client's CPA amends a return covering a locked period
corrections in the open period accumulate to a level that distorts current reporting

nodes.definition: Assemble at year end exactly what the client's CPA needs to do their work, and nothing that pretends to be their work. The package contains the final trial balance for the year, reconciliation reports for every cash and liability account, year-end statements and amortization schedules for loans, the fixed-asset additions and disposals list with the underlying documents, payroll reports from the provider, subledger agings, the open-item list with the treatment applied to each, an extract of the rulebook entries covering judgment calls the CPA previously answered, and a written list of the questions the practice could not and should not answer. It is sent only on the client's written authorization and framed as bookkeeping-side output for the CPA's review, never as a tax-ready or assured product. Adjusting entries that come back are entered as given and tagged as CPA adjustments so they stay distinguishable from the practice's own work, and any adjustment that reveals a standing gap becomes a rulebook or chart-of-accounts change so the same adjustment is not needed again next year.

included: the contents of the bookkeeping-side year-end package
the authorization and framing rules for sending it
tagged intake of returned adjusting entries
conversion of recurring adjustments into standing rules
excluded: preparing or reviewing any return, or forming a tax position
advising the client on what their CPA should do
assurance language of any kind about the package

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: what CPAs request that the package lacked, and which adjustment classes repeat year over year

pros.claim: A complete, well-framed package makes the practice easy for CPAs to work with, which is how bookkeeping reputations are built
pros.example: a CPA receiving reconciliations, schedules and a question list rather than a login and a hopeful message

pros.claim: Tagging returned adjustments keeps the practice's own work distinguishable and makes recurring gaps visible
pros.example: the same depreciation adjustment appearing two years running, which converts into a standing schedule and rulebook entry

cons.claim: Year-end packaging concentrates significant effort into the same weeks for the whole book
cons.example: every client's package falling due while the ordinary monthly closes still have to be delivered

cons.claim: A helpful package can be mistaken for tax-ready work unless the framing is explicit every time
cons.example: a client assuming the year-end package means their return is essentially prepared

failure_modes: sending the package to a CPA without the client's written authorization
including or implying a tax position or an assurance conclusion
entering returned adjustments untagged so practice work and CPA work become indistinguishable
acceptance_tests: the package contains the trial balance, reconciliations, schedules, provider reports, agings, open items with treatments and the question list
every transmission traces to a written client authorization and carries the bookkeeping-side framing
returned adjusting entries are entered as given, tagged, and reviewed for a standing rule change
revisit_triggers: the CPA asks for something the package did not contain
the same adjustment class returns in consecutive years
a client engages a new CPA with different requirements

edges.why_related: the charter decides which systems a subscription close must touch, which is what the provisioning runbook has to supply access to
the charter names the data the practice will hold, which is the material the confidentiality rule governs
the charter's standing refusals are only meaningful once the boundary classifies what is refused
the diagnostic cannot inspect what it cannot see, and a verified connection is what makes its findings trustworthy
the findings register with its severities is the raw material the cleanup scope and its effort units are built from
the review establishes which prior balances have support, which decides where a defensible anchor can be placed
the agreed period and deliverable define what the ordered passes are actually working through
reconciling forward is only stable once the starting balances are fixed and labelled
a coding rule can only point at an account that the standard has defined
connection monitoring operates on exactly the connections the runbook provisioned and recorded
the ordered passes are what generate the unresolved items the queue then carries and ages
the runbook records the rulebook exceptions that make this client's close different from the standard one
the acceptance pack must state how every unresolved item was treated, which only the queue can supply
the recurring calendar starts only once the gate is acknowledged, so the gate sets the first cycle's date
reconciliation can only start once the cutoff has passed and the period's inputs are in
reconciling against a broken or duplicated feed produces a difference that is an artifact rather than a finding
reviewing categories before the population of transactions is settled means reviewing the wrong population
the review is what surfaces the ambiguous items that routing then assigns to a lane
nothing may appear in a packet that the support file cannot stand behind
sign-off is performed against the assembled packet and its traceability, so the packet must exist first
a period is locked at the moment it is signed off and delivered, and defects logged afterwards drive the correction path
the year-end package is assembled from locked, delivered periods, and CPA adjustments come back through the correction path
the boundary limits the note page to factual description and forbids any recommendation on tax, entity, financing or pricing
the boundary's two columns are exactly what decides whether a question may be answered in-house or must be routed
the package may only be transmitted on a written client authorization naming the recipient and the material
the anchor fixes the earliest period the practice may correct at all, which bounds every correction decision
the runbook may record the access path and role level but never a credential or security answer
the published delivery date pulls toward closing now while unanswered client questions pull toward waiting
edges.resolution_rule: close on the published date with the default treatment applied, the item left visible in the holding account and the gap disclosed in the packet - unless the unanswered item leaves a reconciliation unexplained or a balance-sheet line unsupported, in which case the affected statement is held and the client is told the same day

edges.why_related: standardization keeps the book closeable by anyone while each client's reality argues for one more exception
edges.resolution_rule: the standard wins unless the deviation passes the stated test - the owner genuinely manages by that distinction, or a lender, franchisor or their CPA requires it - and every approved deviation is recorded in the runbook with its reason and reviewed on the standard cadence

edges.why_related: an unexplained difference cannot be delivered, but the calendar has promised a date to a client who is waiting
edges.resolution_rule: reconciliation integrity wins: the affected statement is withheld with an explanation of what is unexplained and when it will be resolved, and a forced balancing entry is never an acceptable way to hold the date

edges.why_related: the rulebook exists to stop questions being re-asked while routing exists to stop the practice answering what is not its to answer
edges.resolution_rule: the rulebook may only decide classes the client or their CPA has already answered and whose facts are unchanged; a class never answered, or one whose circumstances have changed, goes to routing however confident the bookkeeper feels

edges.why_related: silent connection breaks are the most common cause of the duplicate, missing and misdirected activity the review pass detects
an anchor accepted without support becomes a permanent unexplainable residue that the support check meets every month
accounts are mapped onto the standard before any month is coded, otherwise the cleanup's coding has to be redone against the standard later
defects classed as rulebook gaps are only worth logging if they change the rulebook before the next close
every answer returned by the client or their CPA becomes a standing rule so the same question is never asked twice
adjustments that recur every year point at a missing account, schedule or policy in the standard rather than at a one-off error
aging items reveal which documents never arrive, which retunes the chasing cadence and the stop rule
both ask the same question - does every balance have something behind it - one at the door and one every month thereafter

conflict_axes.name: standard_process_versus_client_specific_reality
conflict_axes.description: A book of clients is only closeable because every file works the same way, yet every owner has a distinction, a system or a habit that argues for an exception.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the deviation test - genuine management distinction or an external requirement - and record every approved exception in the runbook where it can be counted and reconsidered

conflict_axes.name: delivery_date_versus_unanswered_questions
conflict_axes.description: The published close date is a promise the client schedules around, while unresolved items argue for waiting until the file is genuinely complete.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: deliver with the default treatment and an explicit disclosure unless the gap leaves a reconciliation unexplained or a balance-sheet line unsupported, in which case hold the affected statement and say so immediately

conflict_axes.name: cleanup_depth_versus_client_cost_and_patience
conflict_axes.description: Reaching further back produces a stronger foundation, but each additional period costs the client money and delays the current reporting they actually feel the need for.
poles: clean deeper for a stronger base
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the horizon be set by what the books must support - filings already made, lender or grant reporting, the owner's decisions - and label everything inherited rather than silently absorbing it

conflict_axes.name: automation_throughput_versus_reviewed_judgment
conflict_axes.description: Rule-driven coding is what makes a fixed monthly fee viable, and it is also what spreads a single wrong mapping silently across every month.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: automate only classes the rulebook has settled with a recorded source, mark ambiguous classes as never-auto-post, and let the review pass test the automation rather than the transactions one by one

conflict_axes.name: being_helpful_versus_staying_inside_the_licensed_lane
conflict_axes.description: The bookkeeper is the professional the owner talks to most, so the questions that matter most arrive casually and the helpful answer is often the impermissible one.
poles: route it to the licensed professional
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer factually about what the records show, route anything about treatment or filing with the client's authorization and the client copied, and record the returned answer as a rule

conflict_axes.name: speed_of_setup_versus_least_privilege_access
conflict_axes.description: Owners offer the fastest path into their systems - their own login - exactly when the practice is trying to start work, and proper role provisioning takes longer and feels bureaucratic to them.
poles: start work today with what the client offers
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: least privilege wins without exception; explain the substitute path in one sentence, destroy anything already sent, and record the connection in the access register before work begins

conflict_axes.name: completeness_versus_materiality_in_a_fixed_fee
conflict_axes.description: Chasing every small unexplained amount is what makes books trustworthy, and it is also what makes a fixed monthly fee unprofitable and the client feel interrogated.
poles: apply a documented materiality and disclose
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: resolve anything that affects a reconciliation, a balance-sheet line or a decision the owner is making; for the rest apply the recorded default treatment and disclose it rather than either chasing it or hiding it

conflict_axes.name: stability_of_delivered_numbers_versus_fixing_what_is_wrong
conflict_axes.description: A locked period is what makes reports trustworthy over time, yet errors are found afterwards and leaving them uncorrected is its own kind of dishonesty.
poles: correct at source wherever the error is
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: correct immaterial items in the open period with a note; take material items, and anything behind a filing, to the client and their CPA before reopening, and always reissue with a change note rather than replacing quietly

conflict_axes.name: plain_language_versus_technical_precision_in_reporting
conflict_axes.description: An owner-readable note is what makes the packet worth paying for, while precise accounting language is what keeps it accurate and inside the licensed lane.
poles: write it the way the owner speaks
write it the way an accountant would
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: describe facts in the owner's language and name the accounting term once alongside it, never simplify to the point of asserting a treatment or implying a recommendation

edge_cases.description: Mid-cleanup it emerges that the previous bookkeeper changed transactions in periods that already fed a filed return, so the ledger no longer agrees with what was submitted
edge_cases.trigger: reconciling a period behind the intended anchor reveals post-filing edits
edge_cases.mitigation: stop, document the difference between the ledger and the filed figures, place the anchor at the filing date, and route the question of what to do about the filing to the client and their CPA without touching the period

edge_cases.description: The owner sends their online banking username and password in a message so the bookkeeper can 'just get in and look'
edge_cases.trigger: a client volunteers credentials to speed up onboarding
edge_cases.mitigation: do not use them, tell the client to change the password, record the incident, and send the read-only or accountant-role invitation with a one-sentence explanation of why that path is used instead

edge_cases.description: A bank connection is re-authenticated and silently re-imports six weeks of activity, doubling transactions that were already coded and reconciled
edge_cases.trigger: a feed reconnection back-fills history that already exists in the ledger
edge_cases.mitigation: identify the duplicated range against the statement before deleting anything, remove only the confirmed duplicates, re-run the reconciliation for the affected periods, and record the break so the pre-close check catches the pattern next time

edge_cases.description: The client's CPA returns adjusting entries for a year whose months were all delivered and locked
edge_cases.trigger: year-end adjustments arrive after periods were closed and reported
edge_cases.mitigation: enter the adjustments as given and tagged in the period the CPA specifies, reissue affected reporting with a change note, and convert any recurring adjustment into a rulebook or account-standard change

edge_cases.description: Owner-personal spending runs through the business account in growing volume, and separating it is becoming most of the coding work
edge_cases.trigger: personal and business activity are commingled in the accounts the practice closes
edge_cases.mitigation: code identified personal items to the owner account by rule, queue the ambiguous ones for the owner rather than guessing, disclose the volume in the packet, and route any question about the tax consequence to their CPA

edge_cases.description: Payroll totals in the ledger do not agree to the payroll provider's registers because an integration posts summarized journals
edge_cases.trigger: a payroll integration posts summary entries that cannot be traced to the provider's own reports
edge_cases.mitigation: reconcile the ledger to the provider's registers rather than to the integration's journals, record the mapping in the runbook, and treat any residual liability difference as an open item rather than absorbing it

edge_cases.description: The client goes completely silent through the close window and the cutoff arrives with several unanswered questions
edge_cases.trigger: no client response before the published cutoff
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the client's recorded missed-cutoff rule, post unresolved amounts to the holding account rather than to plausible expense accounts, disclose every gap and default treatment in the packet, and let the aging counters drive the next conversation

edge_cases.description: Processor deposits arrive net of fees, refunds and chargebacks, so revenue and expenses are both understated until settlement reports are used
edge_cases.trigger: a payment processor pays out net rather than gross
edge_cases.mitigation: reconcile the processor account to its settlement report so gross sales, fees, refunds and chargebacks separate, and record the settlement source and timing lag in the runbook

edge_cases.description: The owner asks the bookkeeper to code an obviously personal purchase as a business expense, or to date a transaction into a prior period
edge_cases.trigger: a client requests a recording the records do not support
edge_cases.mitigation: decline to record what the underlying facts do not support, explain that the treatment question belongs to their CPA and the practice records what happened, offer to route the question with the client copied, and record the request and the response

edge_cases.description: A second business the owner runs is transacting through the same bank account and the same ledger file
edge_cases.trigger: commingled activity from a second entity is discovered in the file
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the re-scope trigger rather than absorbing the second entity, separate what can be separated with an inter-entity account that is supported and disclosed, and route the structural question to the client and their CPA

edge_cases.description: A lender, broker or the client's new advisor contacts the practice directly asking for the client's financial statements
edge_cases.trigger: a third party requests client financial data without the client's written instruction
edge_cases.mitigation: send nothing, tell the requester the practice needs the client's written instruction naming them and the material, obtain it from the client, and send only what was authorized in the form authorized

workflow.action: Charter the delivery system and define a finished close
workflow.description: Write the onboarding arc, its exit gate, the deliverable class of a subscription close and the standing refusals before any new file is opened
workflow.artifact: delivery charter with the written definition of a finished close
workflow.gate: the arc stages, the gate that ends onboarding, the deliverable class and the refusals are all stated in one document

workflow.action: Provision least-privilege access and verify every connection
workflow.description: Set up role-based access per system, verify each connection by pulling a known figure through it, and enter everything in the access register with its revocation path
workflow.gate: every system the close touches is connected by role, no client credential is held, and each connection has a verification note

workflow.action: Run the bounded diagnostic and build the findings register
workflow.description: Inspect the incoming file against the standing list and record findings with severity and the work class each needs, without performing any remediation
workflow.artifact: dated findings register capturing the file's incoming condition
workflow.gate: every balance-sheet account has a status, every finding names its work class and severity, and nothing was fixed during the review

workflow.action: Fix and document the opening balance anchor
workflow.description: Choose the anchor date and source, record accepted differences and provided-not-verified labels, and state the rule for anything behind it
workflow.artifact: anchor memo with the trial balance at the anchor date
workflow.gate: date, source, accepted differences and unverified labels are recorded and the baseline trial balance is retained

workflow.action: Scope, price and agree the cleanup as a separate project
workflow.description: Convert the findings register into a written scope with period, deliverable, exclusions, assumptions, measured effort-unit fee and re-scope trigger, accepted before work starts
workflow.gate: written acceptance exists, the fee traces to counted effort units and the practice's own cost-to-serve, and the subscription start point is stated

workflow.action: Map the file onto the niche standard chart of accounts
workflow.description: Map every incoming account to a standard reporting line, decide deviations against the test, and record the mapping before any coding happens
workflow.artifact: old-to-standard mapping table with approved deviations and reasons
workflow.gate: every live account traces to a standard line or a recorded deviation with its reason and approver

workflow.action: Execute the cleanup in the fixed order
workflow.description: Verify history, reconcile cash and card accounts chronologically forward, settle processor and payroll, age receivables and payables, and leave loans, owner accounts and equity last
workflow.artifact: reconciliation reports per account per month across the agreed period
workflow.gate: each month reconciles before its categorization is reviewed and no undocumented balancing entry exists in the period

workflow.action: Work the open items and gate the cleanup
workflow.description: Batch the remaining questions with defaults and ask-by dates, then assemble the acceptance pack with limitations and obtain the client's recorded acknowledgement
workflow.artifact: cleanup acceptance pack with the client's acknowledgement
workflow.gate: reconciliations, handoff trial balance, unresolved items with treatments, assumptions and the statement of what was not done are all present and acknowledged

workflow.action: Write the client runbook and publish the close calendar
workflow.description: Record systems, access paths, connection quirks, deviations, exceptions, contacts, packet composition and landmines, and set the client's cutoff, window and delivery date
workflow.artifact: client runbook with the published close calendar
workflow.gate: a qualified person who has never seen the file could run the close from it, and it contains no credentials

workflow.action: Run the monthly close through reconciliation and review
workflow.description: Check every connection, reconcile each account to its statement or settlement report, then review the coded period against the rulebook and the prior period
workflow.artifact: monthly close file with reconciliation reports and review findings
workflow.gate: every account is reconciled to a third-party document with all differences explained and no forced entries

workflow.action: Assemble balance-sheet support and route judgment calls
workflow.description: Attach named support to every balance-sheet line, run the residue scan, and route anything reserved to the client or their CPA with the routing logged
workflow.artifact: balance-sheet support file with the routing log
workflow.gate: every line has support or a written explanation, the residue scan is clear or disclosed, and no licensed-side determination was made in-house

workflow.action: Build, sign off, deliver and lock
workflow.description: Assemble the packet with factual notes and full disclosure of gaps, have it signed off against the checklist by a second pair of eyes, deliver it and lock the period
workflow.artifact: delivered reporting packet with the sign-off record
workflow.gate: every figure traces to the close file, the notes contain no recommendation, all gaps are disclosed, and the sign-off and lock are recorded

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because the charter, the access provisioning, the confidentiality rule and the licensed-territory boundary decide what may be touched, by whom, and what may never be answered - and every later step inherits those limits. The entry sequence follows because a diagnostic, an anchor and an agreed cleanup scope are what convert an unknown file into a bounded project, and remediation performed before them is remediation performed twice. Standardization of accounts, rules, documents, connections and the client runbook comes next because the recurring close is only repeatable against a standardized file. The close nodes then run in their forced order - calendar and cutoff, reconciliation, categorization review, judgment routing, balance-sheet support, packet - because each one's output is the next one's input and inverting any pair creates rework. The control nodes close the loop last: sign-off and the defect log prove the close happened as specified, the period lock protects what was delivered, and the year-end package hands bookkeeping-side output to the licensed professional while feeding every recurring adjustment back into the standards above.

dominance_rules.rule: Confidentiality and least-privilege access dominate speed and client convenience in every onboarding and close decision
dominance_rules.rationale: an exposed credential or an unauthorized disclosure cannot be undone and puts the client's whole financial position at risk, while a delay costs days
dominance_rules.trigger: any moment where accepting a credential, using a personal channel, or sending data without written authorization would be faster
dominance_rules.action: refuse the fast path, use the provisioned route or obtain the written instruction, and record what was refused and why

dominance_rules.rule: The licensed-professional boundary dominates client pressure and the bookkeeper's own confidence
dominance_rules.rationale: an unlicensed determination can carry consequences for the client's filings that the practice cannot carry for them, however obvious the answer seemed
dominance_rules.trigger: a request touching deductibility, taxability, classification, elections, filings, entity structure or assurance
dominance_rules.action: state what the practice can do, route the treatment question with the client's authorization and the client copied, and record the answer as a rule

dominance_rules.rule: An unexplained reconciliation difference dominates the delivery date
dominance_rules.rationale: reconciliation is the only step that proves the ledger against the outside world, so delivering over an unexplained difference delivers an unknown
dominance_rules.trigger: a difference remains unexplained when the delivery date arrives
dominance_rules.action: withhold the affected statement, tell the client the same day what is unexplained and when it will resolve, and never post a forced balancing entry to hold the date

dominance_rules.rule: A recorded client or CPA answer dominates the bookkeeper's inference on any treatment question
dominance_rules.rationale: the practice's job is to apply decisions faithfully and record their source, not to substitute its own judgment for the person who owns the consequence
dominance_rules.trigger: the rulebook and a fresh inference disagree, or the facts behind a recorded answer have changed
dominance_rules.action: apply the recorded answer, or re-route the question if the facts have changed, and never overwrite a sourced decision silently

dominance_rules.rule: The practice standard dominates client preference unless the deviation passes the stated test
dominance_rules.rationale: a book of clients stays closeable, coverable and reviewable only while the files work the same way
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for an account, report or process that departs from the standard
dominance_rules.action: apply the deviation test, approve only genuine management distinctions or external requirements, and record every approved exception in the runbook

dominance_rules.rule: The agreed cleanup scope dominates informal expansion of the catch-up project
dominance_rules.rationale: absorbed remediation is invisible unpaid work that also destroys the boundary between the project and the subscription
dominance_rules.trigger: discovery of work outside the agreed period, deliverable or exclusions
dominance_rules.action: fire the re-scope trigger, pause, agree the change in writing, and resume only after acceptance

dominance_rules.rule: Named support dominates presentation in everything that is delivered
dominance_rules.rationale: a report that looks right without support is more dangerous than an obviously incomplete one because it will be relied upon
dominance_rules.trigger: a balance-sheet line has no reconciliation, schedule, provider report or written explanation behind it
dominance_rules.action: hold the line's inclusion, obtain or write the support, and disclose it as unsupported if it must be delivered at all

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure dominates appearance whenever a close is imperfect
dominance_rules.rationale: a client who learns later that a month was closed over a gap loses trust in every month, including the sound ones
dominance_rules.trigger: any gap, default treatment, assumption or corrected prior figure in a delivered period
dominance_rules.action: state it plainly in the packet note and in any reissue, rather than smoothing it into the numbers

dominance_rules.rule: The opening balance anchor dominates the urge to correct inherited history
dominance_rules.rationale: periods behind the anchor may support filings and reports the practice cannot see, so changing them can create consequences no bookkeeping judgment can weigh
dominance_rules.trigger: an error is found in a period behind the anchor
dominance_rules.action: document it, leave it untouched, and route the question to the client and their CPA with the evidence attached

anti_rework_rules.rule: Provision and verify every connection before the diagnostic begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole findings register and cleanup scope built on partial feed history that has to be redone once the missing months appear

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix and document the opening balance anchor before reconciling any month forward
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-reconciling months whose starting balances move when the real anchor is finally settled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map the file onto the standard chart of accounts before coding a single transaction
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recoding an entire cleanup period after the standard is applied late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile a month to its statement before reviewing that month's categories, and reconcile chronologically forward rather than newest month first
anti_rework_rules.prevents: categorizing a transaction population that changes when missing or duplicated activity is discovered, which is the most common repeated work in a catch-up

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the cleanup scope in writing before any remediation is performed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unpaid absorbed work and a later renegotiation of what the project was ever supposed to include

anti_rework_rules.rule: Batch client questions into one queue with default treatments instead of asking as items appear
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a client who stops replying to a drip of messages, which turns one close into several partial attempts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the rulebook entry at the moment a judgment call is answered
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the same question being re-asked every month and answered differently by different closers

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the client runbook before the first unsupervised close
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a second closer reconstructing the file's quirks under deadline and producing a close that must be reworked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the connection and integration check before the close window opens rather than when a reconciliation fails
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering a break mid-close and having to redo coding and reconciliation inside the delivery window

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is found after delivery by the client, the next reviewer, or the CPA
iteration_protocol.action: log it with its cause class and convert that class into a change to the rulebook, the runbook, the pre-close check or the checklist before the next close of that file

iteration_protocol.trigger: an access near-miss, a credential offered or accepted, or a disclosure request from an unauthorized party
iteration_protocol.action: re-provision to least privilege, have the client change anything exposed, record the incident, and review the confidentiality rule with everyone who touches client files

iteration_protocol.trigger: a request lands on the licensed boundary and the answer given was improvised
iteration_protocol.action: restate the boundary classification and the referral wording, add the request class to the routing lanes, and check whether anything already recorded needs correcting

iteration_protocol.trigger: cleanup discovery contradicts the assumptions the scope rested on
iteration_protocol.action: stop work, re-scope in writing against the change mechanism, and resume only once the client has accepted the revised project

iteration_protocol.trigger: the open-item queue ages past its carry limit for two consecutive periods
iteration_protocol.action: take the queue to the client as a decision about inputs and cadence, tighten the intake and chasing cadence, and record whether the file still fits a standard close

iteration_protocol.trigger: a connection or integration changes behavior, or duplicated and missing activity is found after a close
iteration_protocol.action: repair the connection, re-verify the affected history against statements, update the failure catalogue and the client's runbook entry

iteration_protocol.trigger: the client's CPA returns adjusting entries or overturns a recorded treatment
iteration_protocol.action: enter the adjustments as given and tagged, update the rulebook entry with the new source, and change the account standard where the gap is general rather than client-specific

iteration_protocol.trigger: delivery dates are missed, or closes are repeatedly delivered with disclosed gaps
iteration_protocol.action: measure the actual close durations and input arrival times, restage the client in the window or fix the input dependency, and only then re-publish the calendar
